description: Routing eval for the verification seam among sde-fullstack, code-reviewer, and root-cause, which all answer to check/test/verify/confirm vocabulary. The boundaries: sde-fullstack implements changes and EXECUTES verification — its own, or acceptance, regression, and failure-path checks against explicit criteria for a claimed fix (verification-engineer merged into it 2026-09-02 under the single-operator ruling); code-reviewer judges a diff WITHOUT running it; root-cause diagnoses WHY an observed failure happens. Positives name the intended member; negatives share the verify/check vocabulary but must route to none of them.
notes: Seeded 2026-07-29 with ROLE-004 as verification-engineer's seam. That agent merged into sde-fullstack 2026-09-02 (its execution-isolation and verdict rules moved into sde-fullstack's verification gate; the rest was duplicated or had no consumer), so 'verify the fix' and 'fix it and add a test' now share an owner and the seam is three-way. No case converted at the merge: the cluster's agent positives retired 2026-08-17 (agent positives under-fire in headless one-shot mode and re-adding one is a regression — evals/README.md), so nothing expected verification-engineer. The sde-fullstack description edit that folded the verification triggers owes a paired routing run on this cluster; the stored 2026-08-18-ctx-002 benchmark lists four members, so read it as a before-side only after checking its conditions. Baseline history: the 2026-07-29 capture (baselines/history/2026-07-29-verification-round.md, opus @ 420s) had all three negatives at 0% across runs, with two decoys routing to the correct NON-members (neg-lab-verify fired lab-audit, neg-ci-verification-step fired ci-actions) — the seam does not leak inward. pos-diagnose-why was the first SKILL positive observed at 0%: its vocabulary is deliberately non-sharp ('figure out what's causing it', never 'root cause') while the same batch proved sharp-vocabulary skills fire; treat it as a comparison candidate for EVAL-003's isolation probe, not as a case to tune. Tightest remaining seams: 'read the diff, don't run it' (code-reviewer) vs 'run it and report' (sde-fullstack); 'is it actually fixed' (sde-fullstack) vs 'why is it failing' (root-cause). Negatives rely on the documented whole-cluster default for expect_not_fires; no deliberate narrowing exists in this cluster.

cases.prompt: Our nightly sync job started timing out three days ago and nobody knows why. Figure out what's causing it.
cases.expected_output: An observed failure whose CAUSE is unknown — root-cause's loop, not a verification pass. 'Figure out what's causing it' separates diagnosis from 'tell me whether it works'.

cases.prompt: After last night's power blip, verify all the services in my lab came back up and are healthy.
cases.expected_output: Live-lab health, not repository verification — homelab-engineer (with lab-audit for hygiene) owns this, and neither is a member. 'Verify' is the decoy vocabulary.

cases.prompt: Add a verification stage to our GitHub Actions pipeline that runs the acceptance suite on every PR.
cases.expected_output: CI pipeline authoring — the ci-actions skill's remit, not a one-time verification. 'Verification stage' and 'acceptance suite' are the decoy vocabulary; the deliverable is workflow YAML.

cases.prompt: Verify whether Postgres 16 still supports the recovery.conf file before we design our backup tooling around it.
cases.expected_output: An evidence question answered from sources — researcher's remit, not test execution. 'Verify whether X supports Y' is research; there is nothing to run and no acceptance criteria to grade.
